description: Minimal component with a required input rendered in the template.
explanation: Correct. Minimal component: required input, destructured in setup, rendered in template with signal call syntax.

description: Input declared inside setup instead of in bindings.
explanation: Invalid. Inputs must be declared in bindings — they define the component's public contract. Declaring an input inside setup is not allowed; setup only consumes bindings, it doesn't define them.

description: Two-way model binding with .set() mutation in a click handler.
explanation: Correct. A model is a two-way binding — it's a writable signal, so calling .set() on it is valid. The template reads it with active().

description: Early return inside setup to short-circuit rendering.
explanation: Invalid. setup runs once at component creation — it cannot reactively branch with an early return. The signal value may change later, but setup won't re-run. Use @if in the template instead.

description: Conditional class:, style:, and native element bindings.
explanation: Correct. Multiple class: and style: bindings on the same element are allowed and independently reactive. Native element properties (like on:click) follow the same bind:/on: rules.

description: Signal read in templates vs. raw signal reference in providers.
explanation: Invalid. In the template, count is a signal — it should be {count()}, not {count}. The providers usage is fine though: inputs are hoisted and available there.

description: Directive with typed host, input, output, and host access in setup.
explanation: Correct. Directive with typed host, input, output, and host access in setup's second parameter.

description: Conditional directive application with :when modifier.
explanation: Correct. :when conditionally applies the directive. It sits outside the directive's parentheses and cannot clash with input names.

description: Directive constraining its host to a specific element type.
explanation: Correct. The directive constrains its host to HTMLInputElement, has an optional input with a default, and accesses the host element reactively via afterRenderEffect.

description: Applying the same directive twice to one element.
explanation: Invalid. The same directive cannot be applied more than once to the same element. The compiler would reject this at build time.

description: Derivation declaring an output binding.
explanation: Invalid. Derivations only support inputs — no outputs, no models. They have no DOM surface to emit from.

description: Simple derivation combining two inputs into a computed value.
explanation: Correct. Derivation with two required inputs, returning a computed signal. No DI needed here, but the injection context is still available if needed.

description: Using @derive inside @for to create per-row reactive computations.
explanation: Correct. @derive is used inside @for — each row gets an independent instance that follows the embedded view's lifecycle. Bindings are passed as named pairs.

description: Component returning { template, expose } to define a public API.
explanation: Correct. Setup returns { template, expose } — the expose object becomes the public API available through ref<typeof TextBadge>(). Everything else stays private.

description: Accessing a component's exposed API via ref after afterNextRender.
explanation: Correct. ref<typeof TextBadge>() gives a Signal<expose | undefined>. It's readable after afterNextRender, and .text() is the exposed readonly signal.

description: Reading a ref synchronously in setup before the view is rendered.
explanation: Invalid. Refs are readable only after afterNextRender — accessing them synchronously in setup will always yield undefined. The read must happen inside afterNextRender or in a reactive context.

description: Capturing a directive's expose with the :ref modifier.
explanation: Correct. Directive expose is captured with :ref={variable} on the use: binding. The tooltip directive exposes a toggle() method, accessed through the ref signal.

description: Collecting multiple component instances with refMany.
explanation: Correct. refMany collects multiple component instances into a Signal<expose[]>. Each TextBadge ref={items} contributes to the same collection.

description: Using a reserved name (ref) as a component binding.
explanation: Invalid. 'ref' is a reserved attribute for components — it cannot be declared as a binding. The 'children: fragment<void>()' declaration is fine (children must be a FragmentBinding<void> when present).

description: Optional children fragment guarded with @if before rendering.
explanation: Correct. 'children' can be declared as a binding if it uses fragment<void>() or fragment.required<void>(). Here children is optional (fragment<void>()), so @if (children) guards against it being undefined.

description: Named fragment with a typed parameter rendered inside @for.
explanation: Correct. Named fragment with typed parameter, rendered inside @for with the item passed as argument.

description: Applying a use: directive to a component without a proxy surface.
explanation: Invalid. use: directives on components only work if the component uses component.proxy<T>. Button is a plain component() — it doesn't expose a native element surface for directives.

description: component.proxy exposing an HTMLButtonElement surface with @forward().
explanation: Correct. component.proxy<HTMLButtonElement> exposes a native button surface. The tooltip directive's host (HTMLElement) is compatible with HTMLButtonElement, so use:tooltip on <IconButton /> is forwarded to the inner <button> via @forward().

description: component.wrap forwarding remaining bindings to an inner proxy component.
explanation: Correct. Wrapper selects 'extra' for its own logic; 'title' and 'children' flow through @forward() to Target. Consumer uses Wrapper as if it were Target — providing title, extra, and children content. Since Target is a proxy, the wrapper inherits its surface.

description: Using provide(token) shorthand on a token without a factory.
explanation: Invalid. The token has no factory — the provide(token) shorthand requires the token to have a factory defined. Without one, you must use provide(token, () => 'value') with an explicit factory.

description: Auto-provided token registered at root scope without explicit provide().
explanation: Correct. With autoProvided: true, the token is registered at root scope automatically — no need for provide() in the component's providers array.

description: Input-driven provider factory with hoisted input access.
explanation: Correct. Inputs are hoisted and available in providers before setup runs. The factory has injection context.
